JAMES BOAST FOR WSJ
 

Do you have too much money in too few stocks—or not enough?

 

For years now, investors have been fretting that the U.S. stock market is overconcentrated in a handful or two of such giant winners as Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft. Could you be underexposed to them instead?

 

That’s the pitch behind a batch of new exchange-traded funds with supersize holdings of the biggest stocks in U.S. industry sectors. Whether you should buy one of these ETFs depends much less on how they’re built than on how you’re built.

 

And most investors should approach all sector funds with caution—especially these new extra-strength versions.

 

Below, some of the best analysis and insight from WSJ writers and columnists, the Dow Jones Newswires team and occasionally beyond, on investing, the wealth-management business and more.

 
 
 

Planning & Investing

 

The Easy Money Offers That Disguise a Deathtrap for Small Businesses

 

Merchant cash advances deliver quick funding, but some carry effective finance costs as high as 2,000%.

 
 
 

Market Talk

 

From Dow Jones Newswires

 

Europe and Canada are expected to keep seeking other partnerships to reduce their dependence on the U.S. regardless of whether there are big Democratic wins in the midterm elections or if the U.S. elects a Democratic president next, Anand Sundar, special adviser to the director of the European Council on Foreign Relations, says. “The message has gotten through that this America is fundamentally different and this is not just about Trump.” There is more of a trend toward less U.S. involvement in the world, particularly in Europe, and conversations in Democratic foreign policy circles are different from what they were during Obama’s presidency, he adds. (Edith Hancock, edith.hancock@wsj.com)

 

Risks of the U.K. interest rates staying higher for longer than markets previously expected are rising as the energy supply disruption persists, Deutsche Bank’s Maui Brennan and Sanjay Raja say in a note. The BOE is widely expected to increase interest rates next week, and markets price in three more BOE interest rate rises by July 2027, LSEG data show, due to inflation fears. “Much will depend on the duration of the unfolding energy shock and how it propagates through the economy – including any signs of second-round effects,” they say. (Miriam Mukuru, miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
